Device fixtures were recorded on 2026-11-05 with the frozen Xcode devicectl and configured physical phones. Raw command arguments, outputs, app results and crash files remain only in ignored build/private storage outside results.

The Task 12 list/unlock fixtures retain parser-relevant fields from live responses. Both phones returned passcodeRequired=false and unlockedSinceBoot=true. The locked fixture is explicitly derived by setting passcodeRequired=true; no live locked response was obtained. The sibling profile.plist is entirely made up.

Task 13 install, launch, await-exited, processes, terminate, copy-from, copy-crash, copy-missing and crash-logs fixtures retain selected fields from genuine direct CLI captures on the first configured phone, before implementing the lifecycle methods. Identifier and executable-container components are placeholders; application bundle IDs, crash filenames and host destinations are scrubbed. Process IDs, outcome/error codes and modification timestamps are retained. The processes fixture retains the app and one unrelated system process. The crash fixture retains two genuine regular-file records with scrubbed names; no SyncBench report was present. Positive timestamp/name filtering uses those records without claiming they are benchmark crashes. A real individual crash file was copied privately to capture copy-crash.

await-timeout.txt records the actual return code, stdout, stderr and selected JSON fields from waiting on the idle app with --timeout 5. This tool rejects --timeout 1 during argument validation because its minimum is five seconds; that rejection is retained privately, separately from the genuine timeout. The wrapper uses the CLI minimum and an independent subprocess deadline to preserve shorter caller limits.

malformed.json is deliberately derived from the install response by replacing installedApplications with null. Further malformed/error test documents are controlled test inputs, not claimed live captures. The copied smoke result and marker were checked with the real CLI: completed and accepted. The second configured physical phone was separately built, installed and launched successfully after developer trust was enabled.
